sentences.text:
The present appeal is filed by the appellantFood Inspector challenging the impugned  judgment and order rendered in Criminal Case No.19/2003 by the Metropolitan Magistrate, 
Court No.6, Ahmedabad dated 15th March, 2007 recording acquittal of the HC-NIC Page 1 of 3 Created On Tue Oct 13 02:33:51 IST 2015 R/CR.A/2346/2008 JUDGMENT respondents accused for the offence under Section 7(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
2.
Heard learned advocate, Shri Raval for the appellant and learned APP Shri Jani for  the respondent no.3State.
Though served, no one appears for the respondent no.1.
The  respondent no.2 had already expired and case against him was abated.

3. As it appears from the reasons recorded for giving benefit of doubt, the Court below has  considered that the pouch of water manufactured by the respondent no.2 were sold by  the respondent no.1 and, therefore, would be entitled to the benefit  under Section 19(2) of the Act.
4. Though the reasons are recorded, learned advocate, Shri Raval submitted that the bills are  not produced providing for any such warranty.
He emphasized that the bill produced  a t t h e t i m e o f h e a r i n g a t M a r k A a l s o d o e s n o t c o n t a i n s u c h  warranty.
He, however, fairly stated that Section 19(2)(a) of the Act would be attracted as  t h e r e s p o n d e n t n o . 1 h a d p u r c h a s e d t h e a r t i c l e s f r o m  the manufacturer.

He submitted that it is not in dispute that the respondent no.2 was a  l i c e n c e d m a n u f a c t u r e r f r o m w h o m t h e r e s p o n d e n t n o . 1 h a d  purchased and sold the pouch of water.

5 . T h e r e f o r e c o n s i d e r i n g t h e p r o v i s i o n s o f t h e A c t , 
particularly, Section 19(2)(a) of the Act that the vendor shall not be deemed to have  committed an offence if he has purchased the articles from the licence manufacturer.

Thus as  he had purchased admittedly from the respondent no.2, who is HC-NIC Page 2 of 3 C r e a t e d O n T u e O c t 1 3 0 2 : 3 3 : 5 1 I S T 2 0 1 5 R / C R . A / 2 3 4 6 / 2 0 0 8 J U D G M E N T licenced manufacturer, he would be entitled to the benefit under Section 19(2)(a) of the Act.
The burden is discharged with regard to this provision.
6. Therefore this Court is in broad agreement with the findings and conclusion arrived  at by the Court below, which does not call for any interference in the present appeal.

7. Moreover, the Hon'ble Apex Court has laid down broad guidelines with regard to the  approach in acquittal appeals in catena of judicial pronouncement and, therefore  considering the aforesaid provisions, it does not call for any interference.
8 . I n t h e c i r c u m s t a n c e s , t h e p r e s e n t a p p e a l d e s e r v e s
to be dismissed and accordingly stands dismissed.
